questions.q: The graph shows $g(x)=|x+4|-2$. State the coordinates of its vertex and the range of $g$.
questions.answer: The vertex occurs where $x+4=0$, i.e. $x=-4$, giving $g(-4)=0-2=-2$. Vertex: $(-4,-2)$. Since $|x+4|\geq0$ for all $x$, the range is $g(x)\geq-2$.
Case 1: $3x-2=7\Rightarrow x=3$. Case 2: $3x-2=-7\Rightarrow x=-\dfrac{5}{3}$. Solutions: $x=3$ or $x=-\dfrac{5}{3}$.

Case 1: $x+5=2x-1\Rightarrow x=6$. Check: $2(6)-1=11\geq0$ and $|11|=11$ ✓. Case 2: $-(x+5)=2x-1\Rightarrow-3x=4\Rightarrow x=-\dfrac{4}{3}$. Check: $2\left(-\dfrac{4}{3}\right)-1=-\dfrac{11}{3}<0$, which cannot equal a modulus (always $\geq0$), so this is extraneous. Only solution: $x=6$.

Subtract 3: $-|x+2|>-4$. Multiply by $-1$ and reverse the inequality: $|x+2|<4$. So $-4<x+2<4$, giving $-6<x<2$.

questions.q: The graph shows $y=|x^2-4x|$. Explain why the parts of the original parabola $y=x^2-4x$ between $x=0$ and $x=4$ appear reflected upward.
questions.answer: $y=x^2-4x=x(x-4)$ is negative for $0<x<4$ (the parabola dips below the $x$-axis between its two roots). Taking the modulus reflects any portion of the graph where the original function is negative upward across the $x$-axis, so that dipped section is flipped to lie above the axis, while the parts where $x^2-4x\geq0$ are unchanged.

questions.q: Explain the difference between the graphs of $y=|f(x)|$ and $y=f(|x|)$, using $f(x)=x-2$ as an example.
questions.answer: $y=|f(x)|=|x-2|$ takes the graph of $y=x-2$ and reflects only the part that lies below the $x$-axis (where $x<2$) upward, leaving the part where $x\geq2$ unchanged. $y=f(|x|)=|x|-2$ instead replaces the graph for $x<0$ with a mirror image of the $x>0$ portion reflected across the $y$-axis, discarding the original left-hand definition of $f$ entirely and producing a graph symmetric about the $y$-axis.
Let $y=3x+2$. Solve for $x$: $x=\dfrac{y-2}{3}$. So $f^{-1}(x)=\dfrac{x-2}{3}$.
Let $y=\dfrac{2x+1}{x-3}$. Then $y(x-3)=2x+1\Rightarrow yx-3y=2x+1\Rightarrow x(y-2)=3y+1\Rightarrow x=\dfrac{3y+1}{y-2}$. So $f^{-1}(x)=\dfrac{3x+1}{x-2}$.

questions.q: Explain why $g(x)=x^2-6x+5$ (domain all reals) is not one-to-one, and state a suitable restricted domain that makes $g$ invertible.
questions.answer: $g(x)=(x-3)^2-4$ is a parabola symmetric about $x=3$, so two different $x$-values equidistant from $3$ give the same output (e.g. $g(2)=g(4)=-3$), meaning $g$ is not one-to-one over all reals. Restricting the domain to $x\geq3$ (where $g$ is strictly increasing) makes $g$ one-to-one and hence invertible.

questions.q: Using the restricted domain $x\geq3$ from the previous problem, find $g^{-1}(x)$ for $g(x)=(x-3)^2-4$, and state its domain.
questions.answer: Let $y=(x-3)^2-4$, so $y+4=(x-3)^2$. Since $x\geq3$, take the positive root: $x-3=\sqrt{y+4}$, so $x=3+\sqrt{y+4}$. Thus $g^{-1}(x)=3+\sqrt{x+4}$, with domain $x\geq-4$ (matching the range of $g$).

questions.q: For $h(x)=(x+2)^2$ restricted to $x\leq-2$, find $h^{-1}(x)$ and state its domain.
questions.answer: Let $y=(x+2)^2$. Since $x\leq-2$, $x+2\leq0$, so take the negative root: $x+2=-\sqrt{y}$, giving $x=-2-\sqrt{y}$. Thus $h^{-1}(x)=-2-\sqrt{x}$, with domain $x\geq0$ (matching the range of $h$).

$(2x-5)^2=(x+1)^2\Rightarrow4x^2-20x+25=x^2+2x+1\Rightarrow3x^2-22x+24=0$. By the quadratic formula: $x=\dfrac{22\pm\sqrt{484-288}}{6}=\dfrac{22\pm\sqrt{196}}{6}=\dfrac{22\pm14}{6}$. questions.q: Solve $|2x+1|=x+4$, checking both solutions are valid.
questions.answer: Case 1: $2x+1=x+4\Rightarrow x=3$. Check: $x+4=7\geq0$ ✓, and $|7|=7$ ✓. Case 2: $-(2x+1)=x+4\Rightarrow-3x=5\Rightarrow x=-\dfrac{5}{3}$. Check: $x+4=\dfrac{7}{3}\geq0$ ✓, and $\left|-\dfrac{10}{3}+1\right|=\left|-\dfrac{7}{3}\right|=\dfrac{7}{3}$ ✓. Both solutions are valid: $x=3$ or $x=-\dfrac{5}{3}$.

sections.heading: A well-designed word problem: calibrating a sensor

questions.q: This question has three parts. An engineer models the deviation of a sensor reading from its calibrated target as $d(x)=|3x-12|$, where $x$ is the applied voltage (volts) and $d(x)$ is the deviation (millivolts). (a) Find the voltage at which the deviation is zero. (b) The sensor is "within tolerance" when $d(x)\leq6$. Solve this inequality to find the acceptable range of voltages. (c) For $x\geq4$, define the calibration function $c(x)=d(x)+2x-5$. Explain why $c$ is invertible on this restricted domain, and find $c^{-1}(x)$.
questions.answer: (a) $|3x-12|=0\Rightarrow3x-12=0\Rightarrow x=4$ volts. (b) $|3x-12|\leq6\Rightarrow-6\leq3x-12\leq6\Rightarrow6\leq3x\leq18\Rightarrow2\leq x\leq6$. (c) For $x\geq4$, $3x-12\geq0$, so $d(x)=3x-12$ without needing the modulus sign flip. Then $c(x)=(3x-12)+2x-5=5x-17$, which is linear with positive slope $5$, hence strictly increasing and one-to-one, so $c$ is invertible on $x\geq4$. Let $y=5x-17$: $x=\dfrac{y+17}{5}$. So $c^{-1}(x)=\dfrac{x+17}{5}$, with domain $x\geq3$ (since $c(4)=20-17=3$).
